pages.title: A Note from Craig Jones
pages.html:
A Note from Craig Jones

I built the PLT Framework before I had a name for it.

It started on a block in Amityville, New York. Watching how things worked. Watching how people made decisions — about money, about relationships, about what they would and wouldn't do, what it cost them, what it gave them. I was running calculations before I had the language for calculation. I was tracking Profit and Love and Tax before those words meant what they mean to me now.

What I learned on that block, and in the years that followed, is this: every mistake a person makes is a calculation error. Not a character flaw. Not a failure of willpower or intelligence or worthiness. A calculation error. The wrong variable weighted too heavily. The cost not seen until it arrived. The gain measured in money when the real gain was in trust. The loss measured in money when the real loss was in time.

This book is the entry point. The twelve mistakes in here are not the twelve mistakes of weak people. They are the twelve mistakes of people who are smart enough to build something real but haven't yet had access to the framework that makes the building accurate.

Lakeema and I built this together. She saw the framework the way only a partner can see it — from the inside, where the costs are most visible and the compound interest on the right decisions is most personal.

Run the full calculation. On everything. Starting now.

Craig Jones

Founder, PLT Framework

Amityville, New York

pages.title: The PLT Framework
pages.html:
The PLT Framework

What it is. Why it works. How to use it.

Every decision you make is a three-variable equation.

Profit. Love. Tax.

Profit is what you gain. Not only money. Skill, time, reputation, peace, optionality, freedom, creative output — these are all forms of Profit. The mistake most people make is measuring Profit in only one currency while ignoring the others.

Love is the relational variable. Trust. Loyalty. Connection. The emotional infrastructure that holds systems together. The energy that moves between people in any transaction, professional or personal. Love is not soft. Love is the most structural variable in the framework. Systems without it are fragile. Systems with it compound.

Tax is the real cost. Not the advertised cost — the actual cost. Time. Stress. Opportunity cost. Health. Relationship cost. The Tax you calculate accurately before you commit is a number you prepared for. The Tax you didn't see coming is the one that collects you.

P + L − T = Your Actual Result. Run this equation on everything.

The PLT Framework was developed by Craig Jones from years of observation, survival, and rebuilding — across street economics, personal finance, business, and relationships. It is not a theory. It is a system that has been tested in the hardest classrooms available.

This book introduces you to the twelve most common places the calculation goes wrong. Each chapter names a mistake, explains the calculation error underneath it, and gives you the correction.

You don't need to read it in order. Start with the mistake that costs you the most right now.

MISTAKE One

01

You Are Solving for Money

When money is one variable and you are treating it like the whole equation.

You took the job because it paid more.

Or you stayed in the business because the revenue was growing. Or you chose the client because the contract was largest. Or you ended the relationship because the financial situation was wrong. Or you didn't end it because the financial situation was wrong in the other direction.

In every one of these decisions, money was the primary variable. Maybe the only variable you ran the calculation on fully.

And some of those decisions worked. And some didn't. And the ones that didn't — when you trace them back — the money was fine but something else wasn't. The culture was wrong. The relationship was transactional. The growth in revenue came with a cost in time or health or integrity that the revenue didn't actually cover.

This is the most common calculation error in the PLT Framework.

Solving for money and calling the solution complete.

Money is one form of Profit. It is the most visible form — which makes it the most over-weighted variable in most people's decisions.

The full Profit calculation includes: financial return, skill development, time leverage, reputation growth, network expansion, creative freedom, peace of mind, and identity alignment. That is eight variables. Most people count one.

The Tax calculation includes: time cost, stress cost, opportunity cost, relationship cost, health cost, and integrity cost. Most people count zero.

When you add the Love variable — what the decision builds or costs in trust, loyalty, and relational infrastructure — you have the complete equation.

Run it completely. Every time.

RCC 001 The job that pays more but costs you your peace is not a raise. It is a loan with a hidden interest rate.

RCC 002 At a certain threshold, more money does not move the quality of your life. Identify your threshold. Then stop trading everything else for money above it.

RCC 003 Every dollar you earn in a configuration that doesn't compound your skills or your reputation is a dollar with no interest attached.

MISTAKE Two

02

You Are Not Naming the Tax

The cost you do not calculate does not disappear. It compounds.

The Tax is the most underestimated variable in the framework.

Not because people are careless. Because the Tax is frequently invisible at the point of decision. It arrives later, in forms that are difficult to connect to the original choice. The stress from the job you took two years ago. The relationship damage from the boundary you failed to hold six months ago. The opportunity you missed because you were too depleted from the wrong configuration to see it when it passed.

Every time you make a decision without calculating the Tax, you are borrowing against a future you haven't priced.

The Tax you refuse to name is the Tax that collects you.

The Tax comes in six forms. You need to account for all six before you commit to anything significant.

Time Tax — Hours and days and years that cannot be recovered.

Stress Tax — The cognitive and emotional load carried by the decision.

Opportunity Cost Tax — What you give up by committing to this path rather than another.

Relationship Tax — The trust and connection cost in the people around you.

Health Tax — The physical and mental cost of the configuration.

Integrity Tax — The cost of decisions that require you to be less than honest with yourself or others.

Total the Tax before you commit. If the Profit plus the Love return is proportional to the full Tax, the decision may be right. If it isn't — you are about to borrow against your future self at an interest rate you have not agreed to.

RCC 004 Name the Tax before you sign anything. The unnamed Tax arrives on a schedule the contract didn't show you.

RCC 005 The Tax you defer by staying in the wrong configuration is not avoided. It is compounding.

RCC 006 If you cannot calculate the Tax of a decision, you are not ready to make the decision. Get the information.

MISTAKE Three

03

You Are Treating Love as a Soft Variable

The most structural force in the framework is the one most people dismiss.

Love is not sentiment in the PLT Framework.

Love is the infrastructure variable. Trust. Loyalty. Belonging. The energy that moves between people in any system requiring human cooperation. The lubricant that reduces friction in every transaction, negotiation, and collaboration. The compound that accumulates over decades and depreciates in minutes when mismanaged.

The person who says "this is business, not personal" is making the most expensive category error in the framework. Business is conducted by people. People respond to Love variables. The relationship with your team, your clients, your partners, your market — these are Love variables. They determine whether your calls are returned, whether deals close at the price you need, whether people invest in you before the proof exists.

The practitioner who dismisses Love as a soft variable is running the calculation with their most powerful variable turned off.

Love compounds. It is the highest-returning asset in any domain — financial, professional, personal — because it compounds over the longest time horizon and depreciates the fastest when mismanaged.

Every interaction you have is either building the Love ledger or drawing it down. There is no neutral transaction. Every meeting, every email, every conversation, every commitment kept or broken — it is going into the ledger.

The person whose Love ledger is full can ask for things the person with an empty ledger cannot. The introduction. The second chance. The deal at a better price because the relationship is worth it. The loyalty that holds when a competitor offers more.

RCC 007 Trust is infrastructure. Build it before you need it. It cannot be built during the crisis.

RCC 008 Every commitment you break is a withdrawal from a ledger you need to have full before you can ask for anything.

RCC 009 The relationship you treat as expendable is the infrastructure you will need when everything else fails.

MISTAKE Four

04

You Are Avoiding the Difficult Conversation

Every conversation you keep not having is compounding interest against you.

The conversation is not going away.

This is the thing about avoidance that the avoidance prevents you from seeing. The conversation you are not having is not sitting still. It is growing. The unsaid thing accumulates cognitive weight — the carrying of it takes energy you could be spending on something else. The unresolved situation it is attached to is developing in a direction you are not influencing because you are not in the conversation.

The conversation avoided at Week One becomes the crisis managed at Week Twenty-Four. The same content. Significantly higher stakes. Significantly higher Tax.

The PLT calculation on difficult conversations almost always favors having them. Not because they are easy. Because avoidance is reliably more expensive.

Difficult conversations have a predictable cost: the discomfort of saying the honest thing. This cost is real and it is finite. You feel it, you get through it, the information moves, the situation changes.

pages.title: The PLT Framework (cont. 2)
pages.html:
Avoidance has a different cost structure: growing cognitive load, progressive relationship damage from the unresolved situation, and the eventual crisis that arrives because the avoided thing was never addressed. This cost is also real. It is not finite. It compounds.

The PLT practitioner prepares the difficult conversation, opens it with curiosity rather than accusation, and has it. Not because they are fearless. Because they have calculated the cost of not having it.

RCC 010 The thing you didn't say grew. Everything unsaid does.

RCC 011 Open the difficult conversation with a question, not a verdict. You need information before you need to be right.

RCC 012 The courage to have the conversation is cheaper than the Tax of avoiding it. Every time.

MISTAKE Five

05

You Are Buying Approval

Being liked and being trusted are not the same asset.

You said the comfortable thing.

In the meeting. At dinner. In the conversation where the honest observation would have cost you the warmth of the room for ten minutes and instead you kept the warmth by saying nothing or agreeing when you didn't agree or softening the truth until it was no longer true.

This is the approval purchase. You traded your credibility for the feeling of being liked.

The trade works in the short term. The room is warmer. The friction is avoided. You feel accepted.

What erodes is the thing that takes years to build and minutes to lose: the reputation as someone whose unfiltered judgment can be trusted when the stakes are real. The person whose honest assessment is sought before important decisions. The advisor who is called when something actually matters.

Every time you suppress an accurate observation to manage the room's reaction, you make a trade: your credibility for the feeling of being liked. This trade is almost always unfavorable.

Being liked is a short-horizon asset. It feels good now. It requires constant renewal through continued performance of the likeable version of yourself.

Being trusted is a long-horizon asset. It compounds across years. It survives conflict. It is the foundation of every relationship that has ever carried real weight.

You cannot have both fully. At some point the honest thing and the comfortable thing diverge and you have to choose which asset you are building.

Build the second. The first follows.

RCC 013 Say the honest thing, said well. The discomfort passes. The credibility compounds.

RCC 014 The person who always agrees with you is not your ally. They are managing your approval of them.

RCC 015 Being liked is not a strategy. Being trusted is. Build the second.

MISTAKE Six

06

You Are Treating Time as Renewable

It is the only Tax that cannot be refunded under any circumstances.

Money lost can be earned.

Reputation damaged can be repaired. Relationships broken can be rebuilt. Deals that fell apart can be restructured. Almost every resource in the PLT Framework has a recovery mechanism — a path from loss back to the position you were in before the loss.

Time has no recovery mechanism.

The two years spent in the wrong job. The three years in the wrong relationship. The decade in a configuration that didn't compound — these are not recoverable. The person who lost them cannot get them back. They can only decide what to do with what remains.

Time is the only Tax I cannot negotiate. I spend it accordingly.

The PLT practitioner treats time with a precision they do not apply to money. Not because time is more important than money in all situations. Because time is finite in a way that money is not. The finite resource requires the more rigorous accounting.

Ask yourself: what is this costing me in time? How many hours per week? Multiply by fifty-two. That is the annual cost. Is the Profit and Love return in the equation proportional to that cost?

If not — you are not in a neutral position. You are in a declining one. Every week you remain in the wrong configuration is a week of compounding stagnation against a world that is not standing still.

RCC 016 Two years in the wrong place is not a neutral cost. It is the most expensive line item in your ledger.

RCC 017 Calculate every significant commitment in hours per year. Then ask whether the return justifies the investment.

RCC 018 The person who treats time as renewable will spend it carelessly until the supply reveals itself as finite. Do not wait for the revelation.

MISTAKE Seven

07

You Are Staying Because of What You Have Invested

History is context. It is not a strategy.

You have put too much in to stop now.

This is the sentence that has kept more people in wrong configurations than any other single thought. The job that was wrong two years ago and is more wrong now, but you have given it so much that leaving feels like admission that the giving was wasted. The relationship that has been declining for three years, but the history is so deep that the thought of exiting feels like erasing something real. The business that has consumed five years and is not working, but five years of your life is too significant to walk away from.

Sunk costs are not arguments.

They are history. History tells you what has happened. It does not tell you what will happen. The calculation runs forward on the variables in front of you — not backward on the investment behind you.

The sunk cost is a real loss. The response to a real loss is not to compound it by making additional bad decisions in its name.

Run the forward calculation. What does staying in this configuration cost per month, in every form of Tax? What is the realistic Profit over the next three years? What is the Love variable — what does it build or cost in trust and relationship?

Compare that to the exit calculation. What does exiting cost, one time? Is the one-time exit cost actually smaller than the ongoing monthly cost of staying?

In most cases where the sunk cost trap has been operating for two or more years, the exit calculation is cheaper.

RCC 019 You are not honoring the investment by staying in the wrong thing. You are just staying in the wrong thing.

RCC 020 The exit calculation run honestly is almost always cheaper than the cost of staying wrong for one more year.

RCC 021 What you have already spent does not change what you should spend next. Run the forward equation.

MISTAKE Eight

08

You Are Not Building Before You Need

Every investment made under pressure costs more than the same investment made in advance.

You are looking for investors when you need money.

You are networking when you need a job. You are building your reputation when you are already in the crisis that the reputation was supposed to prevent. You are asking for the introduction after you needed the person, not before.

This is the investment timing error. The most expensive version of every asset in the PLT Framework is the version you acquire under pressure, when you need it, rather than the version you build in advance, before the need.

The best investments are made before the need exists. That timing is the competitive advantage that cannot be replicated by effort alone.

The skill developed before the market needs it costs less and returns more than the skill acquired under competitive pressure. The relationship built before the person becomes valuable to know is worth more in the moment of need than the relationship built after. The reputation established before the opportunity arrives is the reason the opportunity arrives.

Craig Jones developed the PLT Framework from this observation: the people who consistently have access to the best opportunities are not smarter or harder-working than the people who don't. They are earlier. They invested in the skill, the relationship, the reputation — before the price went up. Before the need made the investment visible to everyone.

Start the investment now. Before you need it. The gap between now and the need is the only window where the investment is at its actual price.

RCC 022 Build the relationship before you need the favor. That is the only version of the relationship that makes the favor possible.

RCC 023 Invest in the skill before the market rewards it. After the market rewards it, the investment cost is the competition.

RCC 024 The network you build when you don't need anything is the network that answers when you do.

MISTAKE Nine

09

You Are in the Wrong Room

The environment you stay in longest becomes the person you become.

The room that never challenges you is not safe.

pages.title: The PLT Framework (cont. 3)
pages.html:
It is slowly shrinking you. The standards of the people around you set the ceiling of what you consider excellent. The ambitions of your environment set the ceiling of what you believe is possible for yourself. The conversations you have most regularly shape how you think.

You cannot outgrow an environment that is not growing.

The wrong room is not a room full of bad people. It is a room full of people whose trajectory does not challenge yours. In the wrong room, the most available friction is the pressure to conform — to lower the standard, shrink the ambition, perform at the top of a range that is not the right range.

Your ceiling is often not your limit. It is your environment's limit applied to you.

The PLT assessment of environment is direct: is this room raising or lowering your standard? Is it expanding or compressing what you believe is possible? Are the people in it building toward something that challenges you to build larger?

If the answer is no — the Tax of this environment is being paid daily in the compounding of your potential against a ceiling that is too low.

Audit the four environments you inhabit most: professional, social, physical, and informational. For each one, run the PLT calculation. What is the Profit of this environment? What is the Love variable — does it build you up or average you down? What is the Tax of remaining in it?

Then upgrade the environment that is costing you the most.

RCC 025 The room comfortable enough to never challenge you is not a safe room. It is an expensive one.

RCC 026 You average toward the people you spend the most time with. Choose them with the same care you choose your investments.

RCC 027 A new room requires you to perform at its level. That discomfort is the investment in the person the new room will make you.

MISTAKE Ten

10

You Are Confusing Loyalty with the Refusal to Calculate

The institution is running an economics calculation. Make sure you know what you are running.

You call it loyalty.

The fifteen years at the company. The relationship maintained past the point where the relationship was serving either party. The commitment to the configuration that the evidence stopped supporting two years ago. You call it loyalty and loyalty is a real thing — a genuine force in the PLT Framework, a Love variable with real compounding value when it is earned and real strategic value when it is placed correctly.

But there is a version of loyalty that is not loyalty.

It is the refusal to run the calculation. The unwillingness to look at the equation because looking at it would require doing something with what you find.

The institution you are loyal to is not running a loyalty calculation. It is running an economics calculation. These produce different results at different times.

Genuine loyalty is a choice made after running the full PLT calculation — where staying is still the right answer after the Profit, Love, and Tax have been assessed honestly. This kind of loyalty is rare and valuable and compounding.

The loyalty mistake is the refusal to calculate. The staying because calculation feels like betrayal. Because looking at the equation means risking finding something that demands action.

The institution will make its economics calculation. The company will restructure. The organization will shift priorities. The loyalty that was performed as reciprocal will turn out to have been one-directional when the economics demanded it.

Run the calculation. Loyalty that survives honest calculation is the only loyalty worth giving.

RCC 028 I called it loyalty. It was the refusal to run the calculation. Those are different things.

RCC 029 Loyalty given to something that cannot reciprocate it is not virtue. It is expensive sentiment.

RCC 030 Run the full equation on every commitment you are currently calling loyalty. If the calculation still says stay — stay with everything you have.

MISTAKE Eleven

11

You Are Not Recovering

The system that runs the decisions must be maintained. This is not optional.

Burnout is not a character flaw.

It is a Tax audit failure. The person who runs at above-sustainable capacity without adequate recovery infrastructure is not disciplined. They are deferring a bill. The bill arrives precisely on schedule, with interest, in the form of declining output, diminished creativity, and the inability to access the thinking that was previously available.

The system that generates your results is physical. The quality of your thinking, the depth of your emotional intelligence, the speed of your decision-making — these are functions of the physical system that houses them. A degraded system produces degraded outputs across every domain.

Recovery is not a reward for good work. It is the maintenance requirement of the system that does the work.

The PLT practitioner treats physical recovery with the same non-negotiable seriousness they apply to their most important professional commitment. Not because health is more important than work. Because the quality of the work depends on the health of the system producing it.

Sleep. Movement. Silence. Real rest — not the absence of work, but the deliberate, protected practice that reduces the accumulation rate of stress Tax. These are not nice-to-haves. They are the infrastructure of sustained high performance.

The person who neglects recovery is undermining every other investment they are making simultaneously. Every hour of deprivation is compounding against the output those hours were supposed to produce.

RCC 031 You cannot outperform a system that is charging you while you sleep.

RCC 032 The recovery stack is non-negotiable — not cancelled when work demands it. Build it. Protect it. The work quality depends on it.

RCC 033 Sustainable performance is a system. Heroic performance is a sprint. Design for the system.

MISTAKE Twelve

12

You Are Waiting to Be Ready

There is no version of ready that exists before the beginning.

You are going to start when you have enough money.

Or when you have enough experience. Or when the timing is right. Or when you have the full plan. Or when the kids are older or the market is better or the person gives you a sign or the fear that is currently preventing you from beginning reduces itself to a manageable level.

None of these conditions will be met before you begin.

This is not pessimism. It is the structural reality of how readiness works. Readiness is not a state you arrive at before you begin. It is a state you enter by beginning. The money comes when you are in the configuration that generates it. The experience comes when you are doing the thing that requires the experience. The timing reveals itself as right or wrong only after you have moved and can see what the movement produced.

Ready is not a starting condition. It is a result of starting. Begin with what you have. Readiness follows action, not the other way.

The PLT calculation on waiting is always unfavorable. Every week of waiting is a week of compounding stagnation. It is a week of not accumulating the data that only action produces. It is a week of not making the mistakes that produce the learning that produces the competence that produces the result.

The asymmetric opportunity — the decision with small Tax and large Profit potential — does not wait for you to be ready. It is available until it isn't.

Begin. Run the equation on the beginning. If the calculation says go — go. Readiness is something you build, not something you find.

RCC 034 The version of you that is ready is built by the version of you that begins before ready.

RCC 035 Waiting for perfect conditions is not preparation. It is the most expensive form of avoidance available.

RCC 036 Begin with the equation. What is the actual Tax of starting now versus waiting six months? Calculate it. Then start.

pages.title: Running the Full Calculation
pages.html:
Running the Full Calculation

What comes next.

You now have the twelve places where the calculation goes wrong.

This is the entry point. The PLT Framework goes significantly deeper than twelve mistakes — into the full architecture of how Profit, Love, and Tax interact across every domain of your life, into the specific patterns that different types of people run and the corrections that apply to each, into the compound economics of decisions made over the long horizons that actually matter.

But the beginning is here.

Run the full equation on one decision this week. Not a small one — a significant one. A commitment you are currently inside or considering. Total the Profit in all its forms. Total the Tax in all six forms. Assess the Love variable — what does this build or cost in trust and relationship and loyalty?

Look at the result.

Then make the decision with the full equation visible rather than the partial one you have been using.

That is the practice. It gets more accurate every time you run it. The accuracy compounds. The results follow the accuracy.

Profit. Love. Tax. Run the full equation. On everything. Starting now.

Craig Jones

Founder, PLT Framework

with Lakeema Jones

About the Authors

Craig Jones

Craig Jones is the founder of the PLT Framework — the system of Profit, Love, and Tax that governs decision-making across every domain of human life. Developed over years of direct observation, survival, and building in Amityville, New York and across Long Island, the PLT Framework is not a theory. It is a system tested in the hardest classrooms available and refined into the most practical decision-making architecture in print.

Craig is the author of the complete PLT Doctrine Series, including The Calculation, Know What You Are, The Soul Economy, The PLT Daily, and the PLT 2026 Master Journal. His work is published through The PLT Press.

She brings to the work the specific understanding that only a partner inside the building of something can bring.
